subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu text commands (/stop, /new, /status) no longer bypass queue during active agent run (3.8 regression)

question: Should Feishu whole-message text commands during active runs bypass the Feishu sequential queue only for safe local status-style commands, or also for stateful commands such as `/stop` and `/new`?
rationale: Current main only gives abort-like `/stop` a separate lane and does not create structured text-slash turns for the reported command set; choosing the stateful command boundary affects session ordering and message delivery semantics.

options.title: Choose the stateful-command boundary first
options.body: Keep the issue open, decide which Feishu text commands may bypass active-run queuing, and then adopt or replace the linked fix with tests and proof for that chosen scope.

options.title: Land a narrow safe subset
options.body: Handle only low-risk local commands such as `/status` first and leave `/stop` and `/new` tracked here or in a narrower follow-up.

options.title: Restore all reported commands
options.body: Sponsor a broader Feishu fix that marks authorized command-only text turns and queue lanes for `/status`, `/stop`, and `/new`, with explicit race and delivery proof.

recommendation.title: Choose the stateful-command boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open, decide which Feishu text commands may bypass active-run queuing, and then adopt or replace the linked fix with tests and proof for that chosen scope.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing signal from the latest Feishu source-carrier merge and adjacent command-boundary history.
